summary.name: Transactional System Administration Is Killing Us and Must be Stopped
summary.one_liner: A 2015 USENIX LISA conference talk by Thomas A. Limoncelli arguing that sysadmins should shift from a transactional request-fulfilling model to a service-centric model that maintains automation.
keywords: the practice of cloud system administration
use_cases: Understanding why ticket-driven sysadmin work hurts team value
Planning a move from request fulfillment to maintaining automation
Researching DevOps and SRE management principles
Preparing a case for a service-centric ops structure in an organization
Reading practitioner perspectives from Stack Exchange's SRE team
summary.what_it_does: The page is the abstract and speaker bio for a talk at USENIX LISA 2015 in Washington, D.C. It contrasts the transactional model, where customers make requests and sysadmins fulfill them, with the service-centric model, where sysadmins maintain automation that does the work. The abstract states that Stack Exchange's SRE team has tried to minimize transactional work and adopt DevOps practices for a cooperative relationship with users. The talk is said to cover successes and failures of these attempts and recommend how other organizations can adopt the structure. The page also includes a BibTeX citation entry.
notable: Compares sysadmin work to auto factory robots: maintain the automation rather than doing the work
Based on Stack Exchange SRE team experience with DevOps practices
Speaker is author of The Practice of Cloud System Administration
caveats: Page is a talk abstract; the full talk content and slides are not on this page
Only the abstract is described, so the claimed successes and failures are not detailed here
